VIDEO.title: The Dangerous Sin Religious People Don’t See (Romans 2)
VIDEO.series: The Book of Romans, Every Word (playlist of 28 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Romans 2:1-16 · Episode 4 (#4 of 28 in the playlist)
hand: Possessing the truth is not practicing it
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Romans 2:1-16. Paul turns to 'everyone who passes judgment': those who condemn others while doing the same things (2:1-4). They are storing up wrath for the day of God's righteous judgment, when He will repay each according to his works, the Jew first and also the Greek, for there is no partiality with God (2:5-11). Those without the Law perish without it, those under the Law are judged by it, and it is the doers of the Law who will be justified; Gentiles show the work of the Law written in their hearts (2:12-16).

Two groups: in 1:18-32 Paul described Gentiles, whose sin is outside God's covenant; in chapter 2 'O man' widens to anyone who judges, and 2:17 names the Jew. Leon Morris (quoted): the Jew was committing basically the same sin even though the formal expression was different. 'You are without excuse' (2:1) echoes 1:20 and sets up 3:23.

Paul builds triads: kindness, forbearance and patience (2:4); glory, honor and immortality (2:7); glory, honor and peace (2:10). God's nature, human imitation, divine reward. Shalom is more than a feeling; it is God putting the broken world back together, one soul at a time.

On the Law: sinned without Torah, perish without Torah; sinned under Torah, judged by Torah (2:12). The teacher draws on the principle of greater light, greater accountability (compare Luke 12:48). The measure differs; the verdict without Christ is the same. With Dwight Pryor, he reads the Gentiles of 2:14-15 as Gentile Christians who now have the Spirit and keep the Law's essence, love (Romans 8:3-4; 13:8-10).

Connections: hypocrisy rebuked in 2 Samuel 12:5-7, Psalm 50:16-21, Isaiah 29:13-15 and Jeremiah 7:8-11; God's character in Exodus 34:6-7 and its echoes; the day of wrath in Psalm 62:12, Proverbs 24:12 and more; no partiality in Deuteronomy 10:17; hearers, not doers, in Ezekiel 33:30-32; the Law on the heart in Jeremiah 31.

The lesson: possessing God's truth is not the same as practicing it. God's righteousness is revealed in those who obey Him, not merely those who know about Him. God is not interested in information about His truth but conformation to it (John 14:15). The teacher believes Christians from a Jewish background felt superior to those from a Gentile background, and Paul is leveling the field.
QUOTES: Possessing God's truth is not the same as practicing it. God's righteousness is revealed in those who obey him, not merely those who know about him.
The measure differs, but the verdict without Christ is the same.
God is not interested in information about his truth, but conformation to it.
They will never accept grace till they tremble before a just and holy law.

LSB_QUOTES.text: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, everyone who passes judgment, for in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself; for you who judge practice the same things.
Or do you think lightly of the riches of His kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance?
For it is not the hearers of the Law who are just before God, but the doers of the Law will be justified.

left.text: For since the creation of the world His invisible attributes, both His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood through what has been made, so that they are without excuse.

right.text: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, everyone who passes judgment, for in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself; for you who judge practice the same things.

lines.text: Romans 1:18-32 works as bait. A reader who feels morally superior nods along, wagging a finger at pagan sin. Then Paul turns: you are without excuse too. The same verdict, the same words.

Leon Morris, quoted in the video: the Jew was committing basically the same sin even though the formal expression was different. Sin inside the covenant looks different from sin outside it, but it is sin.

left.text: Then David’s anger burned greatly against the man, and he said to Nathan, “As Yahweh lives, surely the man who has done this deserves to die.

right.text: Nathan then said to David, “You are the man! Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, ‘It is I who anointed you king over Israel and it is I who delivered you from the hand of Saul.

lines.text: David condemns the rich man in Nathan's story and condemns himself. Paul calls out the same hypocrisy because the Lord has done so before: Psalm 50:16-21; Isaiah 29:13-15; Jeremiah 7:8-11.

left.text: But to the wicked God says, / “What right have you to recount My statutes / And to take My covenant in your mouth?

right.text: These things you have done and I kept silent; / You thought that I was just like you; / I will reprove you and state the case in order before your eyes.

lines.text: Reciting God's statutes while living against them: this is the person of Romans 2:3, who 'passes judgment on those who practice such things and does the same.' God's silence was patience, not approval.
Study note (added): Jesus said the same: 'with what judgment you judge, you will be judged' (Matthew 7:2).

left.text: Or do you think lightly of the riches of His kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance?

right.text: Then Yahweh passed by in front of him and called out, “Yahweh, Yahweh God, compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in lovingkindness and truth; who keeps lovingkindness for thousands, who forgives iniquity, transgression, and sin; yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished, visiting the iniquity of fathers on the children and on the grandchildren to the third and fourth generations.”

lines.text: Exodus 34:6 is the central self-description of God in the Old Testament, repeated or alluded to again and again: Numbers 14:18; Nehemiah 9:17; Psalm 86:15; Psalm 103:8; Joel 2:13. Yet God does not ignore justice: 'He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished.'

src.text: to those who by perseverance in doing good seek for glory and honor and immortality, eternal life;

lines.text: Kindness, forbearance and patience (2:4); glory, honor and immortality (2:7); 'glory and honor and peace' (2:10). All belong to God. His kindness should lead people to seek His glory, honor and immortality, and His shalom then moves through His people.
Shalom is more than an inner feeling. In the Bible it is God putting the brokenness of the world back together, one soul at a time, restoring His image in the world.

KINDNESS.title: The day of wrath, without partiality

left.text: If you say, “Behold, we did not know this,” / Does not He who weighs the hearts understand? / And does not He who guards your soul know? / And will not He render to man according to his work?

right.text: For Yahweh your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great, the mighty, and the fearsome God who does not show partiality nor take a bribe.

lines.text: The day of wrath is everywhere in the Old Testament: Psalm 7:9-11; 62:12; 110:5-6; Proverbs 24:12; Isaiah 13:9-11; Jeremiah 17:10; Ezekiel 7:8-9; Joel 2; Zephaniah 1:14-18. God 'will repay to each according to his works' (Romans 2:6), and 'there is no partiality with God' (Romans 2:11).

Charles Spurgeon, quoted in the video: they will never accept grace till they tremble before a just and holy law; therefore the law serves a most necessary and blessed purpose, and it must not be removed from its place.

left.text: For all who have sinned without the Law will also perish without the Law, and all who have sinned under the Law will be judged by the Law.

right.text: but the one who did not know it, and committed deeds worthy of a beating, will receive but a few. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required, and to whom they entrusted much, of him they will ask all the more.

lines.text: Read 'Law' as Torah. Gentiles outside God's covenant with Israel still die, because they still sin; Jews within Torah who sin still die too. Gentiles are judged by the revelation they had: creation (Romans 1) and conscience (2:14-15). Jews are judged by Torah's covenant standard.
The teacher suggests Paul draws on a principle known in Second Temple Judaism: the greater the light, the greater the accountability. The measure differs; the verdict without Christ is the same.

left.text: For it is not the hearers of the Law who are just before God, but the doers of the Law will be justified.

right.text: “Behold, you are to them like a lustful song by one who has a beautiful voice and plays well on an instrument; for they hear your words but they do not do them.

lines.text: God rebukes a people who admire His message but ignore its demands. It reminds the teacher of Hosea 6:6: 'I delight in lovingkindness rather than sacrifice, And in the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.' Keeping up appearances while far from God in the heart.
Who has truly done the Law? According to Romans 3, no one. Possessing the Law won't save; only doing it perfectly would. That is how Paul sets up the need for the gospel.
Study note (added): 'become doers of the word, and not merely hearers who delude themselves' (James 1:22).

left.text: in that they demonstrate the work of the Law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness and their thoughts alternately accusing or else defending them,

right.text: “But this is the covenant which I will cut with the house of Israel after those days,” declares Yahweh: “I will put My law within them, and on their heart I will write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people.

lines.text: The main line runs from 2:13 to 2:16; verses 14-15 are an aside. Why include it? The teacher, with Dwight Pryor, reads these Gentiles as Gentile Christians: by nature without Torah, but now with the Holy Spirit, keeping Torah's essence, which is love (Romans 8:3-4; 13:8-10; Matthew 22:37-40).
He grants Old Testament support for both readings: all people bear God's image and can obey aspects of the Law, and the new covenant promises the Law written on the heart (Jeremiah 31).

The punchline: Christians from a Jewish background may have felt superior to those from a Gentile background. Paul removes the 'home field advantage': there is neither Jew nor Greek, for all are one in Christ Jesus (Galatians 3:28).

TERMS.def: No defense before God; said of Gentiles (Romans 1:20) and of the one who judges (Romans 2:1).
God's restraint that is meant to lead to repentance (Romans 2:4), rooted in Exodus 34:6.
The day of God's righteous judgment (Romans 2:5); in the prophets, the day of Yahweh.
Wholeness; God putting the broken world back together (Romans 2:10).
God's instruction given to Israel; 'without the Law' and 'under the Law' (Romans 2:12).
The inner witness that accuses or defends (Romans 2:15).
God does not favor anyone for who they are (Romans 2:11; Deuteronomy 10:17).

Conscience; moral awareness. Look up: BDAG, συνείδησις.
Slow to anger; literally 'long of nostrils.' Look up: HALOT or BDB, אָרֵךְ.

BACKGROUND.p: Paul's 'O man' addresses an imaginary conversation partner, a style teachers of the day used. It lets him voice objections and answer them; it is a way of teaching, not an attack on one person.

The Roman church had believers from Jewish and Gentile backgrounds. After Jews returned to Rome following Claudius's expulsion (Acts 18:2), tensions over the Law and food (Romans 14) are easy to imagine.
Israel kept repeating God's self-description from Exodus 34:6-7 in prayer and prophecy: Moses (Numbers 14:18), the Levites (Nehemiah 9:17), the psalmists and Joel.

Paul says plainly that God 'will repay to each according to his works' (2:6) and that 'the doers of the Law will be justified' (2:13). How this fits justification by faith (3:28) is one of the letter's great questions; the video deliberately holds that for later.

DEBATES.p: Gentiles in general, who by conscience do some of what the Law requires (Chrysostom: 'by the reasonings of nature'); or Gentile Christians who have the Spirit and the Law written on their hearts (Dwight Pryor and the video). The teacher notes Old Testament support for both.

DEBATES.h: 'The doers of the Law will be justified' (2:13)
DEBATES.p: A real path no one completes (setting up 3:20-23); a description of the Spirit-led obedience of believers; or a statement of the standard of final judgment. The video holds Paul's use of 'justified' for later.
Any moralist, Jew or Gentile, or specifically the Jew named in 2:17. The video sees the Jewish-background believers in Rome behind it.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: Among the echoes of Exodus 34:6 the video lists 'Psalm 105:45,' which speaks of keeping God's statutes. Psalm 145:8 ('Yahweh is gracious and compassionate; Slow to anger') is probably meant.
The video says eternal life is in 'verse 8'; it is Romans 2:7.
The captions spell 'Dwight Prior'; the teacher is Dwight Pryor.
The 'greater light, greater accountability' principle is presented as rabbinic; the video does not cite a source, so treat it as a summary, not a quotation.
CJB and CGB are the video's own shorthand (Christians with a Jewish or Gentile background), not terms from scholarship.

QUESTIONS: Where are you most tempted to judge others for sins you also commit in a different form?
How has God's kindness led you to repentance?
What does 'greater light, greater accountability' mean for someone who has heard the Bible all their life?
Which reading of 2:14-15 do you find more convincing, and why?
Where is the gap between what you know of God's word and what you do?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: Possessing God's truth is not the same as practicing it. God's righteousness is revealed in those who obey Him, not merely those who know about Him. For the unbeliever, Paul's point is condemnation by works: no one keeps the Law, which sets up the need for the gospel. For the believer, the same principle carries into sanctification: those justified by faith are empowered by the Spirit to do what the Law required. God is not interested in information about His truth but conformation to it. True obedience leaves no room for superiority or a critical spirit toward brothers and sisters; humility should flow from it. 'If you love Me, you will keep My commandments' (John 14:15).
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): before you comment on someone else's failure this week, pray Psalm 139:23-24 and ask where you do 'the same things' (Romans 2:1).

## You who judge
1. Romans 2:1; 1:20: You too are without excuse
   Paul (Romans 1:20, LSB): "For since the creation of the world His invisible attributes, both His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood through what has been made, so that they are without excuse."
   Paul (Romans 2:1, LSB): "Therefore you are without excuse, O man, everyone who passes judgment, for in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself; for you who judge practice the same things."
   (video) Romans 1:18-32 works as bait. A reader who feels morally superior nods along, wagging a finger at pagan sin. Then Paul turns: you are without excuse too. The same verdict, the same words.
   (video) Leon Morris, quoted in the video: the Jew was committing basically the same sin even though the formal expression was different. Sin inside the covenant looks different from sin outside it, but it is sin.
2. 2 Samuel 12:5-7: You are the man!
   David (2 Samuel 12:5, LSB): "Then David’s anger burned greatly against the man, and he said to Nathan, “As Yahweh lives, surely the man who has done this deserves to die."
   Nathan (2 Samuel 12:7, LSB): "Nathan then said to David, “You are the man! Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, ‘It is I who anointed you king over Israel and it is I who delivered you from the hand of Saul."
   (video) David condemns the rich man in Nathan's story and condemns himself. Paul calls out the same hypocrisy because the Lord has done so before: Psalm 50:16-21; Isaiah 29:13-15; Jeremiah 7:8-11. (Isaiah 29:13-15; Jeremiah 7:8-11)
3. Psalm 50:16, 21: My covenant in your mouth
   Asaph (Psalm 50:16, LSB): "But to the wicked God says, / “What right have you to recount My statutes / And to take My covenant in your mouth?"
   Asaph (Psalm 50:21, LSB): "These things you have done and I kept silent; / You thought that I was just like you; / I will reprove you and state the case in order before your eyes."
   (video) Reciting God's statutes while living against them: this is the person of Romans 2:3, who 'passes judgment on those who practice such things and does the same.' God's silence was patience, not approval. (Romans 2:3)
   [Background] Study note (added): Jesus said the same: 'with what judgment you judge, you will be judged' (Matthew 7:2). (Matthew 7:1-5)

## Kindness, patience and the day of wrath
1. Romans 2:4; Exodus 34:6-7: Kindness, forbearance, patience
   Paul (Romans 2:4, LSB): "Or do you think lightly of the riches of His kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance?"
   Moses (Exodus 34:6-7, LSB): "Then Yahweh passed by in front of him and called out, “Yahweh, Yahweh God, compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in lovingkindness and truth; who keeps lovingkindness for thousands, who forgives iniquity, transgression, and sin; yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished, visiting the iniquity of fathers on the children and on the grandchildren to the third and fourth generations.”"
   (video) Exodus 34:6 is the central self-description of God in the Old Testament, repeated or alluded to again and again: Numbers 14:18; Nehemiah 9:17; Psalm 86:15; Psalm 103:8; Joel 2:13. Yet God does not ignore justice: 'He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished.' (Numbers 14:18; Nehemiah 9:17; Psalm 86:15; Psalm 103:8; Joel 2:13)
2. Romans 2:4, 7, 10: Three triads
   Nature, imitation, reward Romans 2:7: "to those who by perseverance in doing good seek for glory and honor and immortality, eternal life;" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+2:7
   (video) Kindness, forbearance and patience (2:4); glory, honor and immortality (2:7); 'glory and honor and peace' (2:10). All belong to God. His kindness should lead people to seek His glory, honor and immortality, and His shalom then moves through His people.
   (video) Shalom is more than an inner feeling. In the Bible it is God putting the brokenness of the world back together, one soul at a time, restoring His image in the world.
3. Romans 2:5-6, 11; Proverbs 24:12: The day of wrath, without partiality
   Solomon's sages (Proverbs 24:12, LSB): "If you say, “Behold, we did not know this,” / Does not He who weighs the hearts understand? / And does not He who guards your soul know? / And will not He render to man according to his work?"
   Moses (Deuteronomy 10:17, LSB): "For Yahweh your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great, the mighty, and the fearsome God who does not show partiality nor take a bribe."
   (video) The day of wrath is everywhere in the Old Testament: Psalm 7:9-11; 62:12; 110:5-6; Proverbs 24:12; Isaiah 13:9-11; Jeremiah 17:10; Ezekiel 7:8-9; Joel 2; Zephaniah 1:14-18. God 'will repay to each according to his works' (Romans 2:6), and 'there is no partiality with God' (Romans 2:11). (Psalm 62:12; Jeremiah 17:10; Zephaniah 1:14-18)
   (video) Charles Spurgeon, quoted in the video: they will never accept grace till they tremble before a just and holy law; therefore the law serves a most necessary and blessed purpose, and it must not be removed from its place.

## Hearers and doers of the Law
1. Romans 2:12; Luke 12:48: Greater light, greater accountability
   Paul (Romans 2:12, LSB): "For all who have sinned without the Law will also perish without the Law, and all who have sinned under the Law will be judged by the Law."
   Jesus (Luke 12:48, LSB): "but the one who did not know it, and committed deeds worthy of a beating, will receive but a few. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required, and to whom they entrusted much, of him they will ask all the more."
   (video) Read 'Law' as Torah. Gentiles outside God's covenant with Israel still die, because they still sin; Jews within Torah who sin still die too. Gentiles are judged by the revelation they had: creation (Romans 1) and conscience (2:14-15). Jews are judged by Torah's covenant standard.
   (video) The teacher suggests Paul draws on a principle known in Second Temple Judaism: the greater the light, the greater the accountability. The measure differs; the verdict without Christ is the same.
2. Romans 2:13; Ezekiel 33:31-32: Hearers or doers?
   Paul (Romans 2:13, LSB): "For it is not the hearers of the Law who are just before God, but the doers of the Law will be justified."
   Ezekiel (Ezekiel 33:32, LSB): "“Behold, you are to them like a lustful song by one who has a beautiful voice and plays well on an instrument; for they hear your words but they do not do them."
   (video) God rebukes a people who admire His message but ignore its demands. It reminds the teacher of Hosea 6:6: 'I delight in lovingkindness rather than sacrifice, And in the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.' Keeping up appearances while far from God in the heart. (Hosea 6:6)
   (video) Who has truly done the Law? According to Romans 3, no one. Possessing the Law won't save; only doing it perfectly would. That is how Paul sets up the need for the gospel.
   [Background] Study note (added): 'become doers of the word, and not merely hearers who delude themselves' (James 1:22). (James 1:22)
3. Romans 2:14-15; Jeremiah 31:33: Written in their hearts
   Paul (Romans 2:15, LSB): "in that they demonstrate the work of the Law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness and their thoughts alternately accusing or else defending them,"
   Jeremiah (Jeremiah 31:33, LSB): "“But this is the covenant which I will cut with the house of Israel after those days,” declares Yahweh: “I will put My law within them, and on their heart I will write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people."
   (video) The main line runs from 2:13 to 2:16; verses 14-15 are an aside. Why include it? The teacher, with Dwight Pryor, reads these Gentiles as Gentile Christians: by nature without Torah, but now with the Holy Spirit, keeping Torah's essence, which is love (Romans 8:3-4; 13:8-10; Matthew 22:37-40). (Romans 8:3-4; Romans 13:8-10; Matthew 22:37-40)
   (video) He grants Old Testament support for both readings: all people bear God's image and can obey aspects of the Law, and the new covenant promises the Law written on the heart (Jeremiah 31).
   (video) The punchline: Christians from a Jewish background may have felt superior to those from a Gentile background. Paul removes the 'home field advantage': there is neither Jew nor Greek, for all are one in Christ Jesus (Galatians 3:28). (Galatians 3:28-29)

## Key people
- 'O man', the one who judges: Anyone who condemns others while doing the same; in 2:17 Paul names the Jew. [Background] The teacher thinks Paul has Christians from a Jewish background in Rome especially in view.
- David and Nathan: David condemns the man in the story and condemns himself. [Background] Nathan's parable of the poor man's lamb follows David's sin with Bathsheba (2 Samuel 11-12).
- Paul: A Hebrew of Hebrews, taught at the feet of Gamaliel; reasoned from the Scriptures in synagogues. [Background] Born in Tarsus and brought up in Jerusalem (Acts 22:3).
- Leon Morris: Quoted: the same sin in a different formal expression. [Background] An Australian New Testament scholar; the video mentions 'his commentary' without a title.
- Dwight Pryor: His view: the Gentiles of 2:14-15 are Gentile Christians. Captions spell 'Prior.' [Background] A teacher on the Jewish roots of the Christian faith; the video gives no source title.
- Charles Spurgeon: Quoted on trembling before a just and holy law before accepting grace. [Background] A nineteenth-century London Baptist preacher; the video gives no source.

## Places [Background]
- Rome: A church of Jewish-background and Gentile-background believers.
- Corinth: Where Paul writes.
- Jerusalem (named in the video): Where Paul studied under Gamaliel; the temple of Jeremiah 7.
- Tarsus: Paul's birthplace in Cilicia (Acts 22:3).
- Mount Sinai (traditional): Where Yahweh proclaimed His name (Exodus 34:6-7). Traditional site; debated.

## Key terms
- Without excuse: No defense before God; said of Gentiles (Romans 1:20) and of the one who judges (Romans 2:1).
- Kindness, forbearance, patience: God's restraint that is meant to lead to repentance (Romans 2:4), rooted in Exodus 34:6.
- Day of wrath: The day of God's righteous judgment (Romans 2:5); in the prophets, the day of Yahweh.
- Shalom (peace): Wholeness; God putting the broken world back together (Romans 2:10).
- Law (Torah): God's instruction given to Israel; 'without the Law' and 'under the Law' (Romans 2:12).
- Conscience: The inner witness that accuses or defends (Romans 2:15).
- No partiality: God does not favor anyone for who they are (Romans 2:11; Deuteronomy 10:17).

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Diatribe: Paul's 'O man' addresses an imaginary conversation partner, a style teachers of the day used. It lets him voice objections and answer them; it is a way of teaching, not an attack on one person.
- Jews and Gentiles in Rome: The Roman church had believers from Jewish and Gentile backgrounds. After Jews returned to Rome following Claudius's expulsion (Acts 18:2), tensions over the Law and food (Romans 14) are easy to imagine.
- Exodus 34 in Israel's prayers: Israel kept repeating God's self-description from Exodus 34:6-7 in prayer and prophecy: Moses (Numbers 14:18), the Levites (Nehemiah 9:17), the psalmists and Joel.
- Judgment by works: Paul says plainly that God 'will repay to each according to his works' (2:6) and that 'the doers of the Law will be justified' (2:13). How this fits justification by faith (3:28) is one of the letter's great questions; the video deliberately holds that for later.

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Who are the Gentiles of 2:14-15? Gentiles in general, who by conscience do some of what the Law requires (Chrysostom: 'by the reasonings of nature'); or Gentile Christians who have the Spirit and the Law written on their hearts (Dwight Pryor and the video). The teacher notes Old Testament support for both.
- 'The doers of the Law will be justified' (2:13) A real path no one completes (setting up 3:20-23); a description of the Spirit-led obedience of believers; or a statement of the standard of final judgment. The video holds Paul's use of 'justified' for later.
- Who is 'O man'? Any moralist, Jew or Gentile, or specifically the Jew named in 2:17. The video sees the Jewish-background believers in Rome behind it.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- Among the echoes of Exodus 34:6 the video lists 'Psalm 105:45,' which speaks of keeping God's statutes. Psalm 145:8 ('Yahweh is gracious and compassionate; Slow to anger') is probably meant.
- The video says eternal life is in 'verse 8'; it is Romans 2:7.
- The captions spell 'Dwight Prior'; the teacher is Dwight Pryor.
- The 'greater light, greater accountability' principle is presented as rabbinic; the video does not cite a source, so treat it as a summary, not a quotation.
- CJB and CGB are the video's own shorthand (Christians with a Jewish or Gentile background), not terms from scholarship.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. Where are you most tempted to judge others for sins you also commit in a different form?
2. How has God's kindness led you to repentance?
3. What does 'greater light, greater accountability' mean for someone who has heard the Bible all their life?
4. Which reading of 2:14-15 do you find more convincing, and why?
5. Where is the gap between what you know of God's word and what you do?

## Application
- (video) Possessing God's truth is not the same as practicing it. God's righteousness is revealed in those who obey Him, not merely those who know about Him. For the unbeliever, Paul's point is condemnation by works: no one keeps the Law, which sets up the need for the gospel. For the believer, the same principle carries into sanctification: those justified by faith are empowered by the Spirit to do what the Law required. God is not interested in information about His truth but conformation to it. True obedience leaves no room for superiority or a critical spirit toward brothers and sisters; humility should flow from it. 'If you love Me, you will keep My commandments' (John 14:15).
- Study note (added): before you comment on someone else's failure this week, pray Psalm 139:23-24 and ask where you do 'the same things' (Romans 2:1).
